rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the already-tested "Maintenance-Light Cash Value" — the only change is RANK→IND_RANK on the identical base and an identical overlay — so it cannot deliver a substantively different economic test.

The base is essentially a free-cash-flow-to-price value proxy (close to published FCF/P), but the pairing with a cash-to-total-liabilities creditor-protection overlay is a coherent and not-yet-tested combination whose stated sign matches the expression's direction.

The oancf/ebitda conversion ratio flips sign whenever EBITDA is negative (a non-trivial share of firms), so the overlay will systematically mislabel loss-makers as poor converters or vice versa, and the second leg (−lct/revt) simply reuses the already-tested liability-intensity overlay.

Economically sensible refinancing-risk conditioner that is distinct from the prior lct/lt overlays by isolating interest-bearing short-term debt, though dlc already enters the enterprise-value denominator so the two legs partially double-count the same variable.

Direct rediscovery of the archived "Cash-Cushion Profit Persistence" with only ni swapped for oancf in the smoothed coverage overlay, and the oancf/lct coverage state was itself already tested in two other archived signals.

Because lct typically dwarfs oancf, the overlay (lct−oancf)/revt is dominated by short-term liability intensity rather than "cash burn," making it a sign-flipped recombination of the already-tested lct/sale overlay rather than the new cash-coverage test the hypothesis claims.
